I haven’t invited any of them to our house for months and I am sure they would love to be here! We need not prepare anything special. Analyze the following case on the basis of your understanding of Edward Hall’s theory of communication styles: (05) Rahael works with United Technologies, a New York based company. She is talking on the phone to Sandeep, the Indian manager of one of United Technologies vendors for customer service outsourcing. Page 2 of 4 Rahael: We really need to get all of the customer service representatives trained on our new process in the next two weeks. Can you get this done? Sandeep: That timeline is pretty aggressive, but we will try our best to do that. Rahael: I think it will require some creativity and hard work, but I think we can get it done with two or three days to spare, right? Sandeep: Yes we may, if we try. Rahael: Now that our business is settled, how is everything else? Sandeep: All’s well, although the heavy monsoons this year are causing a lot of delays getting around the city. Two weeks later… Sandeep: We’ve pulled all of our resources and I’m happy to say that 60% of the customer service representatives are now trained in the new process. The remaining 40% will complete the training in the next two weeks. Rahael: Only 60%? I thought we agreed that they all would be trained by now! Sandeep: Yes. The monsoon is now over so the rest of the training should go quickly. Rahael: Why can’t you complete the task within the deadline? Sandeep: I am certain that it will be done soon. Questions: • What are the reasons for miscommunication? • What are your suggestions to avoid such miscommunication in future? IV. Analyze the following case in terms of your understanding of Hofstede’s Theory on Intercultural Communication. What different cultural dimensions operate in the following society? (08) Ben is a successful Purchasing Manager with a reputation for being hard working and fair. In his regular Monday morning team meeting, the participants are Harry, Charlie, Jim and Sally; Ben gets along with them all and takes their ideas on how to proceed further. The members are free to express any novel techniques employed by them to achieve the goals. After the latest meeting, Ben is surprised when Sally approaches him and complains, "Ben, you have a prejudice against women. First thing in today's meeting, I suggested we consolidate the commodity purchasing into one section, before I was halfway through, you cut in to let Jim speak. By the end of the meeting, you agreed with my idea, but gave Jim all the credit." Ben doesn't know what to think, and besides, he can't even remember Sally bringing up the idea in the first place. "Is something wrong with Sally today?," he wonders, "Why is she making a federal case out of this? This is the problem when you let women take up men’s work. They always make everything an emotional issue." So he makes a joke to minimize the situation, “ Don’t worry Sally, next month I will go for all new ideas and you will lead the team , I promise.’’ Sally gets annoyed and replies, “I am not bothered about what you will do next month. I am not even sure whether I should continue if it goes like this. All I want is to let you know that I am hurt by the way I was treated in the meeting.” Page 3 of 4 V. Analyze the following on the basis of your understanding of communication across cultures: (08) Michael, an American Employee, has been managing a software development team in Delhi for the past two years. He has been working closely with Naina, the Indian team leader, to develop a new networking program. While reviewing his work from the previous week, Michael discovers that he made a mistake in the programming code. He notices that Naina corrected his error, but wonders why Naina did not bring it to his attention so that he could avoid delays and keep from making the same mistake in the future. He asked Naina to meet him in his office to discuss the issue. Naina entered office with a smile on her face and greeted him politely. However, when Michael brought the issue of correction, she began to look sideways and avoided his glance. She apologized for correcting the error and did not explain the reasons for it. Michael stared at her expecting Naina to argue with him over the error. Naina began to feel uneasy and looked down at the floor. Michael felt that she is hiding something from him and got irritated. • How might this behavior be explained? What do you think is taking place? VI.
